title: ECMAScript Abstract Equality (==) Simulator
problemStatement: Implement `abstractEquals(x, y)` implementing the precise ECMAScript loose equality `==` rules without using the native `==` operator. Must handle null/undefined pairs, String/Number coercions, Boolean-to-number conversions, and Object-to-primitive conversions.
interviewTrap: When comparing a Boolean with anything else, the Boolean is coerced to a Number FIRST! So `[] == true` -> `[] == 1` -> `'' == 1` -> `0 === 1` -> `false`.

testCases.name: Compares null and undefined as equal
Coerces number string to number accurately
Handles boolean coercion rules ([] == false is true)

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: The engine coerces primitives via internal algorithms. In loose equality (`==`), boolean values are first coerced to numbers, objects are coerced via `ToPrimitive(hint)`, and `null == undefined` is exclusively true.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for ECMA-262 7.2.14 Abstract Equality Comparison Algorithm.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), ECMA-262 7.2.14 Abstract Equality Comparison Algorithm is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
